entities.name: Oral estradiol
observations: Oral estradiol increases hepatic thyroxine-binding globulin, raising total T4 while reducing the free T4 fraction and potentially increasing levothyroxine requirements in primary hypothyroidism.

entities.name: Calcium
observations: Calcium can bind levothyroxine and reduce its absorption when taken close to the dose; separating administration by 6–8 hours can reverse the TSH increase.

entities.name: Omeprazole
observations: Omeprazole may impair tablet levothyroxine dissolution through increased gastric pH, but randomized evidence found no clinically significant TSH change after 3 months, making this explanation less likely.

entities.name: Hashimoto thyroiditis
observations: Progression can increase thyroid hormone requirements, but it does not explain the simultaneous rise in total T4 as naturally as an estrogen-induced increase in thyroxine-binding globulin.

entities.name: TSH and total T4 rise
observations: After starting oral estradiol, TSH rose from 3.5 to 12.6 mU/mL while total T4 rose from 7.2 to 10.3 μg/dL, a pattern consistent with increased TBG and inadequate free T4 effect.
